title: British Museum collection record for Figure — British Museum (Oc,+.2597)

claims.value: Standing female figure, carved of hard brown wood, very flat: eyes of obsidian surrounded by bone.
'Presented by A.W. Franks Esq. 18 Sept. 1885. Brought by a sailor from Easter Island.' See comment on Oc,+.2595.

Wood from this figure was tested in 2007 to determine the species but no identification was able to be reached. See Catherine Orliac (2007) 'Botanical Identification of 200 Easter Island Wood Carvings'. Leonardo Pakarati, visit to BM, June 2014: Leo described these figures as being related to fertility – the hand across the belly indicates pregnancy, the hand on the vagina relates to impregnation and birth; sometimes a hand to the breast relates to sustenance of the baby.
